did_you_know.text: Did you know? King Ahasuerus promoted Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite and elevated him above all the officials who served with him.
Did you know? The king’s servants at the royal gate were commanded to kneel and bow down to Haman, but Mordecai refused to obey the order.
Did you know? After the king’s servants repeatedly asked Mordecai why he would not obey, they told Haman that Mordecai was a Jew.
Did you know? Haman was not satisfied with harming Mordecai alone; he sought to destroy all the Jews throughout the kingdom of Ahasuerus.
Did you know? Haman cast the pur—that is, the lot—in the month of Nisan, in the twelfth year of King Ahasuerus’s reign. The lot fell on the month of Adar, the twelfth month.
Did you know? Haman described the Jews as a scattered and separate people with different laws, claiming that they did not obey the king’s laws.
Did you know? Haman offered to pay ten thousand talents of silver into the royal treasury if permission was granted to destroy the Jews.
Did you know? Ahasuerus gave Haman his signet ring, thereby granting him authority to act in the king’s name.

Did you know? The decree was written on the thirteenth day of Nisan in the king’s name and sealed with his signet ring, then sent to the officials of the empire in the writing and language of each people.

Did you know? The decree set the same date throughout the empire—the thirteenth day of Adar—and ordered the Jews to be killed, young and old, children and women, and their possessions to be plundered.
Did you know? The couriers set out quickly to spread the decree, while the king and Haman sat down to drink, and the city of Susa was thrown into confusion.
